answer_2.quote: A common test statistic is the difference in accuracy, in which each entry u_n ∈ {1, ..., C} G where C is the number of classes and in this case, G is the maximum length of an entry sequence (or one if each entry has a binary accuracy value). Then g(u_n, v_n) ∈ {-G, ..., G} is the difference in the number of correct predictions between individual entries u_n and v_n.
